issues.t: High-pressure diesel fuel pump fails and contaminates the fuel system
issues.sym: The engine dies or won't start, often with no warning, sometimes after a long crank. It often happens around 100,000 miles.
issues.why: The LML Duramax uses a Bosch CP4.2 high-pressure pump that can wear internally, especially with poor or water-contaminated fuel. When it fails it sends metal through the injectors and fuel lines.
issues.next: Have it towed rather than cranking it repeatedly. Expect the injectors, lines and tank to need cleaning or replacing along with the pump. Use quality fuel and change fuel filters on time to lower the risk.

issues.t: Duramax fuel injectors leak or crack
issues.sym: White or gray smoke, rough idle, hard starting, a rising oil level that smells like diesel, or a 'balance rate' code.
issues.why: The early LB7 Duramax injectors are known to crack and leak fuel into the cylinders or the oil.
issues.next: Check the oil level and smell; fuel in the oil can wipe out the bearings. A full set of injectors is the usual fix.

issues.t: DEF and NOx sensor warnings with a speed-limit countdown
issues.sym: A DEF warning, 'Service Emission System' message, check engine light, and a countdown that limits speed if it isn't fixed.
issues.why: The NOx sensors, DEF heater and pump on the diesel exhaust system fail over time.
issues.next: Have the codes read soon so the truck doesn't go into limp mode. A sensor is the most common fix.

issues.t: Clogged exhaust filter and fuel in the oil
issues.sym: Frequent 'exhaust filter full' messages, power loss, worse fuel economy and an oil level that rises over time.
issues.why: The first Duramax with a diesel particulate filter injects extra fuel to burn the filter clean. Short trips interrupt that process, so the filter clogs and some of the fuel ends up in the oil.
issues.next: Drive at highway speed long enough to let it finish cleaning. Change oil on schedule and check whether fuel is diluting it.

issues.t: Rusted brake lines can burst
issues.sym: The brake pedal suddenly sinks toward the floor, a brake warning light, or wet brake fluid along the frame.
issues.why: The steel brake lines run along the frame and rust through in salted-road areas. Federal regulators investigated this on GM trucks of this era.
issues.next: If the brake pedal sinks, feels soft or goes closer to the floor, or a red brake warning comes on, slow down gently, use a lower gear, and pull over where it's safe. Don't drive on: call for a tow. Have the lines inspected on a lift every year. If any are heavily rusted, replace them before one bursts.

issues.t: Central 'spider' fuel injector misfires
issues.sym: Rough idle, misfires, a check engine light, hard starts or a fuel smell.
issues.why: The 5.7L Vortec V8 uses one central injector with thin lines and small poppet nozzles that clog or leak with age.
issues.next: Have the misfire diagnosed. Replacing the spider assembly is the usual fix, often together with the intake gaskets.

issues.t: Intake manifold gaskets leak coolant
issues.sym: The coolant level drops, a sweet smell, crust around the intake, or milky oil.
issues.why: The intake gaskets on the Vortec V8 break down and let coolant out or into the oil.
issues.next: Don't let it overheat. Replace the gaskets soon and change the oil if coolant got into it.

issues.t: 4-speed automatic slips or shifts hard
issues.sym: Flaring revs between gears, late or harsh shifts, or loss of a gear.
issues.why: The 4-speed automatics in these trucks wear their clutches and seals, and heavy loads and towing heat speed that up.
issues.next: Check the fluid. If it slips, get it diagnosed before damage spreads; adding a cooler helps trucks that tow.

issues.t: Front seat bolts missing or recliner can pinch fingers (recalls)
issues.sym: A front seat that feels loose, or a pinch point near the seat recliner.
issues.why: Some trucks left the factory missing one or two front seat mounting bolts, and the easy-entry seat recliner had a pinch point.
issues.next: Check your VIN for open recalls. A dealer installs bolts or a cover free.

issues.t: Front brake rotors can crack (recall)
issues.sym: Grinding or vibration when braking; in the worst case the wheel can separate.
issues.why: Some front rotors were cast from out-of-spec iron and could crack.
issues.next: Check your VIN for open recalls. A dealer replaces the rotors free.

issues.t: Kinked brake booster hose (recall)
issues.sym: A hard brake pedal or reduced power braking.
issues.why: The brake booster vacuum hose was routed so it could kink.
issues.next: If the brake pedal suddenly turns hard or a red brake warning comes on, press the pedal much harder than normal, slow down, and pull over where it's safe. Don't drive on — call for a tow. Check your VIN for open recalls. A dealer reroutes the hose free.

issues.t: Clunk felt in the steering wheel
issues.sym: A clunk or knock you feel in the wheel when turning at low speed or going over bumps.
issues.why: The sliding intermediate steering shaft loses its lubrication and binds. GM issued a bulletin for it.
issues.next: It's mostly an annoyance, but have the steering checked for loose parts. Lubricating or replacing the shaft fixes it.

issues.t: Broken exhaust manifold bolts
issues.sym: A ticking noise on cold start that fades as the engine warms, or an exhaust smell.
issues.why: Heat cycles cause the exhaust manifold bolts on the 6.0L V8 to snap, which lets exhaust leak.
issues.next: Have it fixed before the leak burns nearby wiring or the manifold warps. Broken bolts often need to be drilled out.

issues.t: Instrument cluster gauges stick or quit
issues.sym: The speedometer, fuel or temperature gauges stick or drop to zero.
issues.why: Small stepper motors behind each gauge fail. GM extended coverage on many of these clusters at the time.
issues.next: A cluster repair shop can replace the motors.

issues.t: Duramax water pump leaks
issues.sym: Coolant drips at the front of the engine, a dropping coolant level or a sweet smell.
issues.why: The water pump seal on early Duramax engines wears and leaks.
issues.next: Keep the coolant topped off and replace the pump before the engine overheats.

issues.t: Overheating while towing
issues.sym: The temperature gauge climbs on hills or when towing, sometimes with reduced power.
issues.why: The LLY Duramax runs hotter than other versions, and a weak fan clutch or clogged radiator makes it worse.
issues.next: Back off and let it cool. Clean the radiator and intercooler and check the fan clutch.

issues.t: Chafed diesel engine wiring harness
issues.sym: Misfire or injector codes, rough running or a no-start.
issues.why: The engine harness on the LLY Duramax rubs against the valve covers and wears through.
issues.next: Have the harness inspected and repaired before replacing injectors.

issues.t: Glow plug module can overheat the glow plugs (recall)
issues.sym: Hard cold starts, a glow plug light, or failed glow plugs.
issues.why: The glow plug control module could keep the glow plugs powered too long and burn them out.
issues.next: Check your VIN for open recalls. A dealer reprograms the module free.

issues.t: Trailer wiring can overheat (recall)
issues.sym: A burning smell or melted wiring near the battery while towing.
issues.why: Too much current through the auxiliary battery feed for the trailer harness could melt its fusible link.
issues.next: Check your VIN for open recalls. A dealer installs a fused harness free.

issues.t: Passenger front air bag inflator can rupture (recalls)
issues.sym: No warning before a crash.
issues.why: Takata-made passenger inflators can break apart when they deploy, sending metal fragments into the cabin. Several recalls cover these years.
issues.next: Check your VIN for open recalls and get it fixed right away. Dealers replace the inflator free.

issues.t: Roof-rail air bag inflator can come apart (recalls)
issues.sym: No warning before a crash.
issues.why: The end cap on the side curtain air bag inflator can come loose or the inflator can rupture when it fires.
issues.next: Check your VIN for open recalls. Dealers replace both roof-rail air bag modules free. NHTSA recall numbers: 20V-736, 21V-504.

issues.t: Brake pedal pivot nut can loosen (recalls)
issues.sym: The brake pedal feels loose or stops working properly.
issues.why: The nut on the brake pedal pivot bolt could back off.
issues.next: Check your VIN for open recalls. A dealer secures the nut free. NHTSA recall numbers: 16V-069, 18V-578.

issues.t: Software fault can switch off the front air bags (recalls)
issues.sym: Usually no sign before a crash.
issues.why: A software diagnostic test in the air bag module could keep the front air bags and belt pretensioners from firing.
issues.next: Check your VIN for open recalls. A dealer reprograms the module free. NHTSA recall numbers: 16V-651, 17V-437.

issues.t: Rear fuel tank can collapse and starve the engine (recall)
issues.sym: The engine stalls or loses power with fuel still showing, on trucks with the dual-tank option.
issues.why: The rear tank could collapse and block fuel from transferring.
issues.next: Check your VIN for open recalls. A dealer replaces the tank free. NHTSA recall number: 23V-047.

issues.t: Engine block heater cord can short and burn (recall)
issues.sym: A burning smell or melted cord when the block heater is plugged in.
issues.why: The block heater cord or terminals could short-circuit, damaging the engine and creating a fire risk.
issues.next: If it happens while you're driving: if you smell burning or see smoke, pull over where it's safe, turn the engine off, get everyone out and well away from the car, and leave the hood closed. Call 911 from a safe spot, even if you can't see flames. Don't drive it again until it has been repaired. Don't use the block heater until the recall is done. A dealer replaces the heater parts free. NHTSA recall numbers: 19V-328, 21V-496.

issues.t: Rear wheels can lock up from a transmission valve fault (recall)
issues.sym: Harsh shifts; in rare cases the rear wheels lock for a moment while driving.
issues.why: Wear in a transmission control valve can cause it to fail. A follow-up recall covers trucks that got the wrong software in the first repair.
issues.next: Check your VIN for open recalls. A dealer installs updated software free.

issues.t: 10-speed automatic valve body faults
issues.sym: 'Service Transmission' warning, harsh or delayed shifts, a bang on downshifts, or the truck stuck in one gear.
issues.why: The valve body in the 10-speed automatic behind the Duramax can wear or fail; GM bulletin 24-NA-188 covers valve body problems.
issues.next: Have it diagnosed promptly and ask about warranty and bulletin coverage; many cases end in valve body or transmission replacement.

issues.t: Diesel DEF and emissions warnings
issues.sym: DEF quality warnings, a DEF heater fault, or a speed-limit countdown.
issues.why: NOx and exhaust temperature sensors and DEF heater parts fail.
issues.next: Have the codes read before the speed limit kicks in. Use fresh, certified DEF.

issues.t: Power tailgate can open by itself (recall)
issues.sym: The tailgate drops open while parked, sometimes unexpectedly.
issues.why: Water gets into the electric release switch and shorts it.
issues.next: Check your VIN for open recalls. A dealer replaces the switch free.

issues.t: Water leaks at the rear window and cab
issues.sym: Wet carpet, stains on the headliner, or water around the sliding rear window and roof marker lights.
issues.why: Owners report water getting past seals at the power sliding window, roof lights and rear cab.
issues.next: Fix it soon to avoid mold and damaged electronics. A shop water test can find the entry point.

issues.t: Gas V8 keeps running after the key is off
issues.sym: The engine keeps running for a moment after you shut it off.
issues.why: Voltage feeds back through the fuel pump module; GM bulletin PIT6489 covers it.
issues.next: Have the dealer check for the bulletin repair.

issues.t: Brake module bolts can let water in and start a fire (recall)
issues.sym: Usually no warning; possible ABS warning light.
issues.why: The brake pressure module bolts may not be tight, letting water in and causing a short.
issues.next: If it happens while you're driving: if you smell burning or see smoke, pull over where it's safe, turn the engine off, get everyone out and well away from the car, and leave the hood closed. Call 911 from a safe spot, even if you can't see flames. Don't drive it again until it has been repaired. Check your VIN. Park outside until the dealer repairs it free.

issues.t: Steering gear shaft can break (recall)
issues.sym: Loose or unresponsive steering.
issues.why: A shaft in the steering gear can fracture and disconnect from the steering arm.
issues.next: Check your VIN for open recalls. A dealer inspects and replaces the gear free.

issues.t: Tire label lists the wrong rear pressure (recall)
issues.sym: No symptom, but the rear tires may be run underinflated if you follow the label.
issues.why: The tire label and settings show a rear pressure that is too low.
issues.next: Check your VIN. A dealer updates software and covers the label free.

issues.t: Owner's manual missing from the radio (recall)
issues.sym: The electronic owner's manual isn't available on the screen.
issues.why: Some trucks left the factory without the manual loaded.
issues.next: Check your VIN. A dealer resets the radio free.
